name: Penalties

subjectOf.text: Noncompliance with a CIA carries serious penalties, because the OIG may prosecute the company or seek its exclusion from federal health care programs.
subjectOf.abstract: Upon noncompliance with the terms of a CIA, the OIG can prosecute the company or seek its exclusion from federal health care programs.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Elizabeth R. Malay, The Role of Corporate Integrity Agreements in the Expansion of Fiduciary Duties (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2317580

subjectOf.text: If the government finds problems on inspection it can escalate beyond the CIA's own substantive provisions to criminal prosecution, fines, additional CIAs, and exclusion from federally funded health care programs.
subjectOf.abstract: These penalties include criminal prosecution, fines, additional CIAs, and exclusion from federally funded health care programs.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Elizabeth R. Malay, The Role of Corporate Integrity Agreements in the Expansion of Fiduciary Duties (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2317580
scope_conditions: government inspection of a company operating under a CIA

subjectOf.text: Adopting a generic compliance program is not sufficient under Rule 206(4)-7: advisers that fail to specifically tailor their compliance program to their own business have incurred large penalties in SEC enforcement.
subjectOf.abstract: Failure on the part of advisers to specifically tailor a compliance program for their business has led to large penalties.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal and Oesterle, The History of Hedge Fund Regulation in the United States (2016). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2714974
scope_conditions: applies to funds subject to Rule 206(4)-7

subjectOf.text: Non-performance reputational penalties in a DAO are entirely free from racial or cultural biases, because the token holders imposing them are unlikely to even know each other.
subjectOf.abstract: Crucially, non-performance reputational penalties are entirely free from racial or cultural biases and associated implications as the token holders are unlikely to even know each other.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Blockchain Solutions for Agency Problems in Corporate Governance (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3373393
scope_conditions: DAOs where token holders are pseudonymous and mutually unknown
